transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate your time. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up a spot from someone who needs it more, because I know you have patients with much more pressing issues. I'm a social worker myself, so I feel like I probably should be better at managing things, but... well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people, or take pleasure in things, has gone very quiet. 

It's probably nothing terrible, I mean, I'm still getting my day-to-day things done. But I used to really love my work, and doing yoga, going to art galleries, even just journaling at home. And lately, I'm mostly just moving through obligations. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or ungrateful, but it just feels a bit flat, if that makes sense? Is that... is that the sort of thing you usually see people for?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I suppose... it's been about eight months now. It started right around the time we moved my older relative into our apartment. Which, I want to be clear, is a good thing! I'm glad we can be there for them, and I really don't want to sound like I'm blaming them for any of this. It's just... that's when I noticed this whole shift in how I'm thinking and working, and how I'm connecting with people. 

I've probably just been letting the stress get to me more than I should, honestly. I'm sure you hear about this kind of thing all the time with caregivers, right? I just hope I'm not overreacting by bringing it up.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I, um... I really wish I could give you a more positive answer. I've been trying, I really have. I still go through the motions—like, I'll sit and watch a movie with my family or try to read a book, mostly because I don't want to bring down the mood in the house. But if I'm being completely honest... no. I don't really feel that spark with anything right now. It's just sort of... blank? 

I feel terrible admitting that out loud, because I know I have so much to be grateful for, and I really don't want to sound like a pessimist. Is that... is that a terrible thing to admit? I just feel like I should be trying harder to snap out of it, you know? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just giving up.
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable?

Oh, um, yes... I think that's sort of what I was trying to explain just a moment ago. With the yoga and the journaling, and going to the galleries... I really used to love all of those things. And now the interest just isn't there at all. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, or making it sound like a bigger deal than it is! I know you have to ask these things to get the full picture. But yes, I've definitely lost that sense of enjoyment I used to have. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day?

I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. I mean, empty might be... a little strong of a word? I definitely have moments where I feel a bit flat, but I try really hard not to let it take over my whole day. I still get up and do what needs to be done for my relative and my family, and I try to keep a smile on my face for them. 

I just... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or wallowing in it. I know everyone gets down sometimes, right? I'm probably just letting the exhaustion catch up with me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Oh, um, no. My weight has been pretty steady, actually. I try really hard to make sure I'm still eating regular meals, you know, just to keep my strength up so I can keep helping out at home. I wouldn't want anyone to worry about me not eating or taking care of myself. 

I mean, my clothes still fit exactly the same. I hope that's a good thing? I know sometimes stress or feeling a bit off can make people drop weight, but I'm really trying my best to stay healthy so I don't become a burden to anyone. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you feel like you're depressed most of the day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say depressed. I mean, like I mentioned, there's that flatness sometimes, but I really try to push through it. I definitely don't feel depressed most of the day. 

In my line of work—being a social worker, you know—I see people who are truly struggling with deep depression, and I wouldn't want to claim I'm going through that when others have it so much harder. I really just try to count my blessings and keep moving forward so I can be there for everyone else. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you happiness?

Well, um... I guess this is actually what finally brought me in to see you. I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my life, because I know I have a lot of good things, but... it's just that the part of me that used to reach out to people, or find joy in things... it's just gone very, very quiet lately. 

I used to love my work, and going to yoga, or walking through art galleries... even just sitting down with my journal. But lately, I'm mostly just moving through my obligations. I do what I need to do, but that spark just isn't there right now. I feel terrible even admitting that, because I know I should be enjoying those things. I'm really trying to get back to normal, I promise. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right without sounding too negative.
Do you feel like you're in a low mood most of the day?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say I'm in a low mood. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself after what I just said about the joy being gone... but it's really not a sad or down feeling. 

I always make sure to keep a positive attitude, especially for my clients and my family. I would absolutely hate to bring anyone else down by walking around in a bad mood all day. It's really just more of that... that quiet or blank feeling I mentioned earlier, rather than actually feeling low or tearful. 

Does that distinction make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture without making things sound worse than they actually are.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite over the past eight months?

Oh, um, no, I haven't noticed any changes there. My appetite has been pretty normal, actually. 

I always try to make sure I eat properly—you know, keeping my energy up so I can be fully present for my clients. I wouldn't want to let my physical health slip and become a worry for my family or anything like that. So, yes, I'm still eating my regular meals and taking care of myself that way. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really do try to do everything I'm supposed to do to stay healthy. Is that the kind of information you need for your notes?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or the way you move throughout the day?

Oh, um, no, I don't think there's been any change there. My energy has been pretty steady, actually. 

I still get up and go to work every day, and I make sure I'm moving around and staying active. I know how important it is to keep a good routine going, so I really make it a point to stay on top of things. I wouldn't want to just sit around or become a burden to my colleagues by slowing down, you know? I always want to make sure I'm pulling my weight.

So, no, I haven't noticed feeling drained or moving any differently. I hope it's helpful that I'm keeping my routine up? I really am trying my very best to stay on track with everything.
Do you often feel guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say I struggle with guilt. I really try to live in a way where I don't have anything to feel guilty about, if that makes sense? 

I mean, I always try my absolute hardest to do the right thing by my clients and my family. If I ever do make a mistake—which, you know, we all do sometimes—I just make sure to apologize and fix it right away. I would hate to let anyone down or carry around that kind of negative energy, so I just focus on doing my best and being helpful every single day. 

So, no, I don't really spend time dwelling on things or feeling guilty. I hope that shows I'm keeping a healthy perspective? I really do want to make sure I'm handling things the right way for you.
Can you think of any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find you have to push yourself to do?

Oh, um... well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I really didn't want to bring it up because I know how important it is to stay positive, but... I suppose that's actually what finally brought me in to see you. 

I just... I feel like the part of me that used to really reach out for people and, you know, take joy in things... it's just gone very quiet lately. I used to absolutely love my work, and going to yoga, visiting art galleries, even just journaling at the end of the day. But now, it feels like I really have to push myself to do any of it. I'm mostly just moving through my obligations, making sure I get everything done so I don't let anyone down. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds ungrateful or negative. I really am trying to push through it and keep up with everything. Is it okay that I shared that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me get back to being my best self.
Do you feel like you're actually feeling sad, rather than just not feeling pleasure, for most of the day?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say I'm feeling sad, exactly. I really try to keep my spirits up and look on the bright side of things. 

I mean, I know I mentioned that things have felt a little... quiet, or flat, I guess? But it's definitely not sadness. I'm not sitting around crying or feeling down in the dumps, I promise. I still smile at my clients and make sure I'm bringing good energy to my sessions, because they rely on me, you know? I wouldn't want to bring any kind of heaviness into my work or my home life. It's more just... a lack of that extra spark I used to have, rather than an actual feeling of being sad. 

So, no, I wouldn't use the word sad at all. I hope that makes sense? I really want to make sure I'm explaining this the right way so you know I'm still trying my best to stay positive.
Do you feel like you're actually feeling sad, rather than just not feeling pleasure, for most of the day, or is it more of a neutral or empty feeling?

Oh, um... well, "empty" sounds a bit... a bit severe, doesn't it? I would hate for you to think I'm just walking around feeling completely empty inside. That sounds like I'm not trying at all, and I really, really am! 

I guess... maybe neutral is a better word? Just sort of... even. Like I'm just going through the motions to make sure my clients and my family get what they need from me. But definitely not sad, and I wouldn't say empty, either. I'm still very much here and trying my absolute best to keep things running smoothly. 

Is it okay that I describe it that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without making it sound worse than it actually is. I'm still doing okay, I promise!
Do you feel like you're in a depressed mood for most of the day?

Oh, um... depressed? No, I really don't think so. I mean, I know that word gets thrown around a lot, but I wouldn't use it for myself. 

I really try to keep a good attitude. I mean, I have to, right? As a social worker, I'm the one who's supposed to be helping other people with their struggles, so I can't let myself get bogged down in a depressed mood. I make sure I get up every day, put on a smile, and do what I need to do. 

I just wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself or letting things fall apart. I'm really not depressed, just... maybe a little tired or flat, like we talked about? I hope that's the right way to answer that. I'm really trying to be helpful and give you the right information.
Do you feel like you're in a low mood for most of the day, even if it's not severe?

Oh, um... a low mood? I guess I wouldn't really call it low, either. I mean, I don't want it to sound like I'm dragging myself around or bringing anyone else down. 

I really do make an effort to stay upbeat, especially for my family and the people I work with. I wouldn't want to be a burden or seem like I'm not handling things well. I'm just... maybe coasting a bit? Just keeping things steady. I wouldn't say it's low, just... steady. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea, because I really am still functioning fine and keeping everything together. I hope I'm answering these questions okay?
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities is mild or moderate?

Oh, um... mild or moderate? I suppose... well, I really don't want to make it sound like I've just given up on everything, because I haven't! I still do all the things I'm supposed to do. 

But... I guess what finally made me come in to see you is that... well, the part of me that used to really reach out for people, or feel that spark of joy in my work, or when I'd go to yoga, or visit art galleries... even just writing in my journal... it's all just gone very, very quiet. 

I'm still doing what I need to do, I promise. I'm just mostly moving through my obligations right now, rather than really... feeling them, I suppose. I'd probably call it mild, though, because I am still doing them! I haven't stopped trying. Is it okay that I explain it that way? I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need without sounding like I'm not making an effort.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities is significantly impacting your daily life?

Oh, um... significantly? I really wouldn't use a strong word like that, because I don't want it to sound like I'm failing. I want to be clear that I am absolutely still showing up to work every single day. I take my responsibilities very seriously. 

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details—it has had a little bit of an effect. Just a little. I've... well, I've missed a couple of grant deadlines recently, which really isn't like me at all. And my supervisor, she's wonderful, she actually stepped in and quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. Just for now, I'm sure. I think she could just tell I'm not quite functioning at my usual level right this minute. 

But I'm still there, and I'm still trying my hardest. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible social worker? I really am still doing my best to hold it all together. Does that answer your question okay?
Would you say your lack of interest in activities is more on the mild side or has it been moderately impacting your daily functioning?

Oh, um... well, I know we just touched on this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record, but... I guess I'd say it's somewhere in between? Maybe leaning towards mild, because like I said, I am absolutely still going to work every day. I'm still showing up. 

But... well, since you're asking about the impact... I suppose I have to admit that it's not totally invisible. I mentioned the grant deadlines I missed, which, again, I feel terrible about. And my supervisor moving those demanding clients... she did it so kindly, but it's because she knows I'm just not quite operating at my full capacity right now. I'm just not my usual self, as much as I'm trying to be. 

So I guess it is impacting things a little bit more than I'd like to admit. I just... I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm doing a bad job overall? I'm still trying so hard to keep everything running smoothly. Is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without making it seem worse than it is.
